edges.label: refines
edges.reason: The NEW quote provides specific legal reasoning (lack of standing for a National Trust member) explaining the "clearing the way" mentioned in the EXISTING quote. This is a more specific detail of the same event.

spans.value: The Supreme Court’s majority held in the ballroom case that one member of the National Trust for Historic Preservation’s “mere offense, disagreement, or distaste” was not enough to qualify for standing — effectively greenlighting the above-ground construction that had been halted by lower courts.

edges.label: same_fact
edges.reason: Both quotes are from the same article (metadata indicates thehill.com) and describe the same Supreme Court ruling that allowed the White House ballroom construction to proceed. The new quote provides the specific legal basis for the ruling.

confirmations.sentence: “The Supreme Court last week cleared the way for President Trump to continue construction of a massive ballroom replacing the White House’s East Wing, removing a major legal hurdle for one of his several beautification projects around Washington, D.C.”

edges.sentence: On 2026-09-07, The Hill reported “The Supreme Court last week cleared the way for President Trump to continue construction of a massive ballroom replacing the White House’s East Wing, removing a major legal hurdle for one of his several beautification projects around Washington, D.C.”; on the same day, The Hill reported “The Supreme Court’s majority held in the ballroom case that one member of the National Trust for Historic Preservation’s “mere offense, disagreement, or distaste” was not enough to qualify for standing — effectively greenlighting the above-ground construction that had been halted by lower courts.”.

On 2026-09-07, The Hill reported “The Supreme Court last week cleared the way for President Trump to continue construction of a massive ballroom replacing the White House’s East Wing, removing a major legal hurdle for one of his several beautification projects around Washington, D.C.”; on the same day, The Hill reported “The construction of a massive White House ballroom is moving full steam ahead after the Supreme Court found a historic preservation group likely had no right to stop it.”.

On 2026-09-07, The Hill reported “The construction of a massive White House ballroom is moving full steam ahead after the Supreme Court found a historic preservation group likely had no right to stop it.”; on the same day, The Hill reported “The Supreme Court’s majority held in the ballroom case that one member of the National Trust for Historic Preservation’s “mere offense, disagreement, or distaste” was not enough to qualify for standing — effectively greenlighting the above-ground construction that had been halted by lower courts.”.
